key_insight: Wall heat losses, together with channel confinement, strongly alter early flame propagation and help trigger tulip and distorted tulip flame shapes in premixed hydrogen-air channels.
engineering_relevance: Accurately modeling wall thermal coupling is important for predicting flame stability, safety, and combustion behavior in confined propulsion and process channels.
method: Direct numerical simulation of fully compressible reactive Navier-Stokes equations
Detailed chemical kinetics and transport for stoichiometric hydrogen-air combustion
Conjugate heat transfer with conductive channel walls and external convective/radiative losses
evidence_signal: The simulations are compared against adiabatic-wall cases and reproduce the main experimentally observed features of flame dynamics in confined channels.
watch_item: Results depend on high-fidelity chemistry, transport, and wall heat-transfer modeling, so lower-order models may miss early-stage flame inversion or tulip formation details.
paper_title: The Effect of Heat Loss During the Early Stages of Flame Propagation and Tulip Flame Formation
